ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: On June 19, 2017, an unexpected incident occurred during the process in which the Long March 3B Yao-28 rocket launched the Zhongxing 9A satellite. Due to an anomaly of the launch vehicle, the satellite did not enter the predetermined orbit according to the original plan. Through the cooperation and efforts of aerospace tracking, telemetry and command personnel, and through multiple orbital adjustments, the satellite successfully changed orbit and entered geosynchronous satellite orbit. The schematic diagram of the satellite orbit-change principle is shown in the figure. The satellite changes speed from the apogee Q of elliptical orbit I to enter the geosynchronous orbit II, and point P is the perigee of the elliptical orbit. Which of the following statements is correct (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The speed of the satellite at point Q on elliptical orbit I is less than the speed at point Q on geostationary orbit II

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The satellite changes orbit from the apogee Q of elliptical orbit I to enter synchronous orbit II. How does the speed at point Q on elliptical orbit I compare with the speed at point Q on synchronous orbit II?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The speed of the satellite at point Q on elliptical orbit I is less than the speed at point Q on geostationary orbit II
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is an outer circular orbit, labeled II; inside the circle there is an elliptical orbit, labeled I. The Earth is located near the focus on the left side of the elliptical orbit, point P is on the left side of the ellipse, indicating the perigee; point Q is at the right end of the ellipse, and is both the apogee of elliptical orbit I and intersects or coincides with the outer circular orbit II. Reasoning: Let the distance from point Q to the geocenter be r. When the satellite passes through point Q on elliptical orbit I, from the vis-viva formula there is v_I^2=GM(2/r-1/a_I). Because Q is the apogee of the ellipse, the semi-major axis of the ellipse a_I<r, so 1/a_I>1/r, and thus 2/r-1/a_I<1/r, that is, v_I^2<GM/r. Synchronous orbit II is a circular orbit in the figure, and the circular-orbit speed at point Q satisfies v_II^2=GM/r. Therefore v_I^2<v_II^2, obtaining v_I<v_II.
